Liquidity for an ETF with a lower percentage of assets trading daily can still be good if the underlying securities are liquid or if the ETF is similar to a very active ETF that can be used for hedging by market makers.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: An ETF's traded volume (ADV) is backward-looking and understates how much can trade. An ETF inherits the forward-looking implied liquidity of its basket: IDTS is the min-over-names of tradable ETF shares, one of four additive liquidity components mapped onto the EBILS grid.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Volume != Liquidity: Implied Liquidity, IDTS & the EBILS Grid
